picks.why: At 16.4x trailing with EPS up 13.4% and one of the lowest volatilities on the list (1.57% weekly), this fortress-balance-sheet bank is cheap, and the synthesis has financials beating SPY for three weeks running on better carry as the front end reprices.
At 11.6x trailing with EPS still up 10.1%, the best underwriter in auto insurance is among the cheapest sound businesses on the table, and a hawkish front end raises the yield on its float.

At 16.9x with EPS up 6.2% and 1.93% weekly volatility, Pepsi is a real staple priced well below its usual multiple, the kind of cheap defensive the synthesis says is being bid while expensive ones like WMT and COST de-rate.

Healthcare is the Council's single biggest opportunity, and at 16.9x Regeneron is the cheapest healthcare name on the table, with a net-cash balance sheet and no GLP-1 franchise, so it is less exposed than most to Monday's MFN pricing announcement.

EPS has doubled (+102.8%), leaving Nucor at 20.2x behind a tariff wall the synthesis judges more durable than any deal, with Canada's counter-tariffs due Sept 8 and one of the strongest balance sheets in steel underneath.

summary: A defensive-leaning value book across five sectors: two cheap financials that hold up if the front end stays hawkish, a discounted real staple, the cheapest non-GLP-1 way into the Council's healthcare opportunity, and Nucor's tariff-protected earnings. I skipped utilities, semis and the AI complex, energy, LLY and rate-exposed REITs; I passed on GOOGL and AMZN because investment gains appear to inflate their trailing EPS, and on HON because its market cap doesn't fit its share price, while FIVE reports this week and was off-limits. I have no memory of how this week went and used none.
